summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was readmitted with shortness of breath, fevers, and dizziness eleven days after discharge to rehab following a fall with rib fractures. Imaging revealed a moderate left pleural effusion, concerning for hemothorax, and a new right lower lobe consolidation suggestive of pneumonia. He was treated for healthcare-associated pneumonia with intravenous vancomycin and cefepime, later transitioned to oral levofloxacin. A chest tube was placed, draining 1200 cc of serosanguinous fluid, with resolution of the effusion and improvement in respiratory status. He developed dizziness and left-sided coordination issues, but MRI brain showed no acute abnormality; neurology attributed symptoms to neuropathy. His hemoglobin dropped to 6.7 g/dL, prompting a single unit of packed red blood cells. His diabetes was managed with adjustment of Lantus dose to prevent hypoglycemia. He was discharged to the same rehab facility on oral antibiotics, pain control, and instructions for slow mobilization due to neuropathy and fall risk.
